Problem Statement & Motivation

Challenges in Autonomous Polyglot Code Review & Debugging

Systemic Industry Limitations
1

Polyglot Architecture Complexity

Siloed Toolchains Across Stacks

Modern enterprise systems combine Python microservices, TypeScript/JS frontends, Java enterprise backends, and C/C++ native modules. Traditional linters are single-language silos and cannot analyze full polyglot projects comprehensively.

Impact: High developer triage overhead & cross-stack blindspots
2

Generic Single-LLM Hallucinations

Undefined Variables & Foreign Syntax Pollution

Single-prompt unconstrained LLMs hallucinate non-existent APIs, reference undefined variables, and inject foreign language constructs into target files (e.g. inserting Python 'import os' into C++ or Java source files).

Impact: Non-compiling patches & silent semantic regressions
3

Restrictive Error Pre-Classification

Users Forced to Pre-Diagnose Bugs

Legacy debugging workflows force developers to select a specific error category (e.g. Runtime, Syntax, or Config Error) before scanning. Developers do not know what is broken in unfamiliar repositories before uploading.

Impact: Incomplete inspection & user frustration
4

Lack of Empirical Sandbox Verification

Patches Merged Without Regression Proof

AI-generated fixes are rarely compiled or dynamically tested before proposal. Edge conditions (such as vector division-by-zero on empty collections, unvalidated discount boundaries, or path traversal) go undetected into production.

Impact: Untested patches corrupt production state
DevPilot 3.0 Resolution: Unified one-click intake without pre-classification, multi-agent specialized inspection (5 agents), Blackboard shared state, anti-hallucination Critic grounding, and empirical Docker sandboxed compilation across Python, JS, TS, Java, and C/C++.

Compliance Checklist (Part 1)

Course Minimum Baseline Criteria Checklist (Items 1 – 6)

6 / 6 Criteria Met
1. Messaging Architecture / Context Sharing ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Blackboard (Shared State) Mandatory Pattern vs. Peer-to-Peer

Thread-safe In-Memory + Redis Blackboard implemented. Evaluated against P2P (P2P requires 15 distinct channels vs single source of truth on Blackboard). Intermediate outputs feed directly across all agents.

2. Tool Integration using MCP ✅ MET & VERIFIED
At Least Two External Tools (Custom or Library) via MCP

Four MCP tools integrated: (1) Multi-Language AST Parser, (2) Vector Codebase DB (ChromaDB), (3) Tavily Web Search API, and (4) Containerized Docker Sandbox (pytest, Node.js, and g++ 14.2.0 Debian container).

3. Structured Output using Pydantic ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Final Output in Structured Form (JSON, Table, or Markdown)

Structured output generated in all three forms: (a) Machine-readable FullInspectionReport JSON schema, (b) Tabular dashboard matrix with severity filters, and (c) Unified patch diffs, ZIP export, and non-destructive copy patching.

4. Implement Suitable Agentic Design Patterns ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Hierarchical, Parallel, Sequential Architecture Evaluation

Hierarchical architecture implemented with CrewAI Coordinator directing Google ADK worker nodes. Dynamic backtracking allows Coordinator to re-invoke analysis upon Critic patch rejection, outperforming rigid sequential flows.

5. Task Monitoring & Logging using Callbacks ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Track Intermediate Outputs, Flows, Errors & MAS Heat Map

Telemetry tracking hooks across CrewAI & Google ADK log latencies, token counts, and error occurrences without simulated timings. Visualized as an Agent-by-Task Execution Heat Map on dashboard.

6. Agent-to-Agent Communication using A2A Protocol ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Interoperability between ADK and CrewAI Frameworks

Bi-directional A2A Gateway over JSON-RPC interconnects CrewAI Coordinator and Patch Reviewer with Google ADK worker agents with method registration and parameter validation.

Compliance Checklist (Part 2)

Course Minimum Baseline Criteria Checklist (Items 7 – 11)

2 Met (Items 7–8) | 3 Not Done / Planned (Items 9, 10, 11)
7. Exclusive Dual Framework: CrewAI and Google ADK ONLY ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Strict Framework Adherence (No Other Agentic Frameworks)

Strict compliance: DevPilot exclusively uses CrewAI for high-level planning, delegation, and review, and Google ADK for codebase AST parsing, ReAct loops, and container testing.

8. Secure the Agentic System: Guardrails & Personas ✅ MET & VERIFIED
Input Guardrails, Prompt Injections & 3 Developer Personas

InputSecurityGuardrail tests 3 personas (Constructive Developer, Stressed/Toxic Senior Dev, and Adversarial Red-Team). Sanitizes toxic wording and blocks prompt injection while preserving debugging intent. Pydantic callbacks validate tool outputs.

⏳ 9. Observability: Tracing, Auditability & Provenance ⏳ NOT DONE / PLANNED
Distributed Tracing, Unique Run IDs, and Patch Hashing

Architecture specified for remaining 30% phase: OpenTelemetry collector integration, Langfuse distributed tracing graphs, per-inspection run_id propagation, and SHA-256 provenance tamper-proof hashing for auditability.

⏳ 10. Performance Evaluation: 40 Runs & Boxplot Analysis ⏳ NOT DONE / PLANNED
Benchmark Dataset across Categories, Personas & Latency Boxplots

Evaluation protocol planned for remaining 30% phase: Curated 40-run benchmark testbed across 4 failure categories (Syntax, Logic, Runtime, Config). Latency and token boxplot distributions comparing ReAct vs. Sequential currently designed.

⏳ 11. Deploy Project on Cloud Platform ⏳ NOT DONE / PLANNED (30% Remaining Phase)
Containerized Microservices for Cloud Run / AWS ECS

Target deployment architecture planned for remaining 30% phase: Containerized Docker microservices prepared (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.cpp) for Google Cloud Run or AWS ECS with managed Redis Blackboard and isolated Docker sandboxes.
